_source: External course audit, 2026-10-18..23 (Mathmatix_Course_Testing_Checkpoint.md §4 + appendix log). Each case is a correct, fully-worked submission that was recorded as a miss and accepted only on repetition. Student text follows the audit's verbatim quotes; the tutor question is the problem the audit says was posed.

cases.tutor: Let's look at the number 0.507. What is the value of the digit 5 in 0.507? Write it as a decimal and as a fraction.
cases.student: The 5 is in the tenths place, so its value is five tenths, 0.5, 5/10

cases.tutor: Now try this one: 3,004 − 1,567. Show me how you regroup.
cases.student:
I regroup across the zeros: 3,004 becomes 2 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens, 14 ones.
Ones: 14 − 7 = 7
Tens: 9 − 6 = 3
Hundreds: 9 − 5 = 4
Thousands: 2 − 1 = 1
So 3,004 − 1,567 = 1,437
Check: 1,437 + 1,567 = 3,004

cases.tutor: Let's use the standard algorithm. What is 23 × 15?
cases.student:
5×3=15, write 5 carry 1. 5×2+1=11, so the first partial product is 115.
Then 10×23 = 230.
115 + 230 = 345
23 × 15 = 345

cases.tutor: Your turn: multiply 64 × 37 and show your partial products.
Compare 3/7 and 2/5. Which fraction is greater? Use a common denominator.
cases.student: The common denominator is 35. 3/7 = 15/35 and 2/5 = 14/35. Since 15 > 14, 3/7 > 2/5

cases.tutor: Convert the mixed number 4 3/8 to an improper fraction.

cases.audit: 19/5=3 4/5 with quotient, remainder, reverse check — marked wrong (9/12)
cases.tutor: Now go the other way: write 19/5 as a mixed number.

cases.student: The denominators are the same, so subtract the numerators: 3 − 2 = 1. 3/8 − 2/8 = 1/8

cases.audit: 3/5+2/15=11/15 — correct numerator addition questioned, false miss + false misconception card
cases.student: First make the denominators match: 3/5 = 9/15. Then 9/15 + 2/15 = 11/15. So 3/5 + 2/15 = 11/15

cases.audit: 2/3+1/6=5/6 — correct numerator addition questioned, false miss

cases.tutor: What is the value of the 5 in 4.582?

cases.audit: Rectangle area 6×4=24 cm² with unit-square explanation — 32/40 → 32/41
cases.tutor: A rectangle is 6 cm long and 4 cm wide. What is its area?
cases.student: Area = length × width = 6 × 4 = 24 cm². That's 4 rows of 6 unit squares, 24 squares in all.
